user_review.method: Maintainer executed a clean, telemetry-disabled project installation from the previous standalone GitHub version and its release demo, then executed the changed walkthrough in a separate disposable folder. Read the generated HTML as the receiving operator and opened the parsed handoff in headless Chrome. No customer or new agent session was measured.

scenarios.request: Install TaskDock and resume from a sample browser handoff.
scenarios.expected: One demo command generates the HTML. The page identifies the approved result and what to verify next.
scenarios.observed: The old demo generated no HTML and its separately exported page led to a generic next step. The changed demo exported the page, identified delivery/release-notes.txt and directed the user to compare runtime-copy.txt and record the check. The comparison and follow-up note were performed on the sample.

scenarios.request: Retry the demo in an occupied directory and resume after a sample folder move.
scenarios.expected: Preserve earlier files, support a fresh output folder, and recover the same task by UUID with the updated state.
scenarios.observed: The occupied demo returned exit 1 and retained all previous file hashes. A fresh output completed. The moved folder was found by its UUID and its regenerated page included the updated state. Reusing an existing report name returned exit 2 and preserved the previous report and source.

scenarios.request: Export a handoff with a pending file move.
scenarios.expected: Return nonzero, show the specific operation and preserve all task files.
scenarios.observed: A real planned move produced a handoff with the operation ID and pending recovery warning, returned exit 1 and preserved every task file hash.

similar_skills.learned: The author's README shows a completed handoff and paste-ready first message. The source workflow specifies a reading order and a concrete next action.
similar_skills.reason: The TaskDock public guide follows a generated release handoff, with the current file and the next check visible in the report backed by the existing task records.

similar_skills.learned: The author provides a runnable dry-run against synthetic data and verifies the source hash afterwards.
similar_skills.reason: Reuse the disposable TaskDock demo, compare actual artifact bytes, and prove a retry and HTML export preserve earlier files. The walkthrough only needs local task records.

similar_skills.learned: A selected path can resume after an identity or branch match is ambiguous, and stale source state is surfaced.
similar_skills.reason: TaskDock identifies movable folders by UUID and already supports explicit paths. The first-use fix leaves branch identity and automatic Git mutations out.

validation.observed: 66 tests: 65 passed, one platform-specific skip. The new regression executes the release demo and checks the generated report against final task records. Reran after using a single path format in the demo rollback assertion and improving error reporting in its subprocess regression.

Generated a real private handoff and a matched sample deliverable, verified rollback conflict handling and unchanged files, opened the refreshed HTML in headless Chrome, and completed the written next step.
Verified normal export after a move and exit 1 with a visible pending operation. Compared source file hashes before and after exports.
TaskDock package, product page and manifest passed the targeted audit.
